name: Courage
definition: Own your decisions, speak up when it is uncomfortable, and admit mistakes openly. Reflect on them rather than defend them.

rows.situation: When you are alone in the room
rows.justRight: Says the thing, once, clearly, with the reason. Then lets the decision be made.
rows.over: Takes the contrary position as a habit, and stops being informative.

rows.under: Waits to see whether anyone notices.
rows.justRight: Says it first, says what it cost, and says what you are doing about it.
rows.over: Confesses so constantly that people cannot tell which mistakes were serious.

rows.situation: When there is nobody to sign it off
rows.under: Waits for permission that was never going to arrive.
rows.justRight: Decides, writes down the reasoning, and tells the people it affects.
rows.over: Decides alone on things that needed other people, and spends the next month unwinding it.

rows.situation: When someone needs to hear something difficult
rows.under: Says it to everyone except them.
rows.justRight: Says it to them, early, in private, along with what you would like to see instead.
rows.over: Delivers hard feedback so bluntly and so often that people stop hearing any of it.

rows.situation: When your decision is questioned after the fact
rows.under: Distances yourself from it, and finds someone else who agreed.
rows.justRight: Owns it, including the part that was wrong, and separates the reasoning from the outcome.
rows.over: Defends it past the point where the evidence has turned.
